title: Budget-Governor inference orchestrator: region-tier selection and GPU sieve
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a Budget-Governor orchestration layer that combines region selection, tier routing, and model-variant fallback into a single policy primitive. The governor enforces per-customer soft and hard spend caps, prefers cheaper spot capacity and lower-cost GPU SKUs when safe, and falls back to on-demand or lower-capacity model variants when budgets or SLOs are threatened. This ticket scopes the routing algorithm, data signals, API knobs for Console, and a minimal rollout plan for Canary customers.
acceptance_criteria: A policy language (JSON schema) exists for: preferred region list, tier ordering, GPU SKU preferences, spot-preference weight, soft/hard budget caps, and fallback model variant mapping.
Controller calculates routing decision within 3ms median overhead per request in staging with 10k rps mix and maintains latency SLOs for tier=latency-critical routes.
When soft budget threshold reached, controller switches batch size and model variant per policy and emits a trace event and metric for the customer showing estimated cost delta.
Hard cap enforcement must drop or queue requests per policy and emit a visible Console alert and billing block for the customer.
E2E tests simulate spot evictions and verify automatic fallback to on-demand region or compatible model variant with <1% error rates introduced.
Console UI exposes budget cap controls, region preferences, and an activity log for routing decisions (with links to trace IDs).
Documentation page and PRD linked, and engineering runbook for incident response created.
technical_notes: Policy primitive: priority list of (region, tier, gpu_class, model_variant) with weights for spot preference and cost-sensitivity coefficient.
Decision inputs: current spend (rolling 24h), per-request estimated token cost, queue depth, node headroom, recent spot eviction rate by region/GPU SKU, customer SLA tier.
Algorithm: scoring function = beta_cost * est_cost + beta_latency * est_latency + penalty(eviction_risk) + hysteresis_term to avoid flapping.

GPU classification: map cloud SKUs into buckets (A: high perf V100/A100X, B: balanced T4/A10, C: low-cost BF16/QAT variants). Controller prefers lower buckets if cost coefficient high and latency budget allows.
Fallbacks: model_variant map includes quantized/latency-optimized builds with quality fingerprints; automated quality gates to prevent silent regressions.
Data plane integration: router returns chosen model_endpoint and injects metadata headers (x-redwood-routing-policy, x-redwood-budget-state) for observability and billing attribution.
Config surface: Console + runtime API to set per-customer caps and per-route overrides. Defaults: soft_cap=80% of monthly commit, hard_cap=100%.
Observability: add metrics routing.decision_time_ms, routing.spot_fallbacks, routing.hard_cap_blocks, and tracing tags for budget state and selected GPU class.
Performance: implement fast-path cache for hot customers to avoid recomputing policy per-token; invalidate on policy change.
Compatibility: must work for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Private will enforce only local-region preferences and ignore cloud SKU mappings.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): unit/integration tests + synthetic load test in staging; validate scoring function against historical trace data (Mar 2025 - Feb 2026).
Phase 1 (alpha): enable for 5 non-critical internal customers with read-only policy override and verbose logging for 2 weeks.
Phase 2 (canary): enable soft_cap enforcement for 25 small customers; monitor error budget and cost deviation; revert knob available.
Phase 3 (gradual): open to opt-in by customers in Console; enable hard_cap only after 2 weeks of stable operations per-customer.
Phase 4: default enablement for new customers with conservative defaults; advanced controls behind feature flag for enterprise tenants.
testing_plan: Unit tests for scoring function with edge cases: zero headroom, extreme eviction risk, transitive model quality drop.
Integration tests mocking spot eviction events and verifying fallback path within 500ms cold-start window.
Load test: 10k rps mixed workloads in staging with metric assertions on routing.decision_time_ms and end-to-end latency SLOs.
Chaos test: inject intermittent region outages and validate routing picks alternate region/tier while preserving per-customer budget constraints.
Regression gate: automatic quality monitoring comparing golden prompts across model_variant fallbacks; block rollout if quality loss > 2% top-level metric.
tradeoffs: Favoring spot/low-cost GPUs reduces unit cost but increases eviction risk; mitigation via hedging and faster fallbacks increases complexity in the routing controller.
Soft caps preserve customer experience at cost of temporarily overspending; hard caps protect budgets at the risk of rejected requests and potential churn.
Per-customer policy complexity increases CPU overhead in routing; we add caching to reduce cost but must handle cache invalidation correctly.
Providing many knobs in Console risks user confusion; default conservative presets required to keep UX simple.
risks: Silent quality regressions when falling back to quantized model variants — must be detected by eval hooks.
Incorrect spend estimation for multimodal workloads may cause premature caps; need improved per-request cost estimation for embeddings and long-context generations.
Latency-sensitive customers could be impacted if controller misranks latency vs cost for a route — include route-level overrides to whitelist critical routes.
Telemetry volume increase from per-decision tracing — will increase observability cost; use sampling and aggregated metrics where possible.
